skills.title: Features That Shape Canada's Image
skills.description: Buildings, landscapes, wildlife, and traditions help make Canada's image, like mountains, prairies, beavers, and fishing towns. Match each feature to the identity or image it gives.

skills.title: Indigenous Gifts to Canada
skills.description: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit people gave Canada art, canoes, kayaks, medicines, and democratic ideas. Match each gift to the people who made it.

skills.title: Newcomer Gifts to Canada
skills.description: Newcomers helped build Canada, like Chinese workers on the railway and the British with Parliament. Match each group to what it gave.

skills.title: Working Toward an Inclusive Canada
skills.description: Many groups have worked so everyone is treated fairly, and laws like the Charter help. Match each group or law to how it helps inclusion.

skills.title: Treaty Land Where I Live
skills.description: Every community in Ontario is on traditional Indigenous land and inside a treaty area. Match a place to its territory and treaty.

skills.title: Why People Came to Canada
skills.description: People came to Canada for freedom, land, jobs, family, or to escape hunger and war. Some were forced to come. Match each person to why they came.

skills.title: Life in Newcomer Communities
skills.description: Newcomers farmed, worked, dressed, ate, and worshipped in ways from their old homes. Match each way of life to where it came from and how it touched Indigenous communities.

skills.title: Kinds of Communities in Canada
skills.description: Canada has Indigenous, French, British, immigrant, religious, resource-town, rural, and city communities. Match each kind to how it helped build the country.

skills.title: Big Events for Indigenous Peoples
skills.description: Treaties, the Indian Act, reserves, residential schools, and the creation of Nunavut changed Indigenous communities. Match each event to how it affected them.

skills.title: Big Events for Newcomer Groups
skills.description: Groups like Acadians, Japanese Canadians, Black Canadians, and Germans lived through big events. Match each event to the group and how it changed them.

skills.title: Jewish Communities in Canada
skills.description: Jewish Canadians built synagogues, hospitals, and groups, and faced antisemitism. Match each event to the year or the way the community responded.

skills.title: How Communities Met and Mixed
skills.description: Communities in Canada traded, made treaties, helped each other, and sometimes faced racism or conflict. Sort examples into helpful or hurtful interactions.

skills.title: How Communities Differ
skills.description: Communities can differ in roles, wealth, city or country life, religion, and beliefs about land. Match each difference to the communities it describes.

skills.title: How My Community Has Changed
skills.description: Your own community, whether a town, a faith, or a culture, has changed over time. Pick the changes that happened and why.

skills.title: What Makes Canada Canada
skills.description: Canada values human rights, diversity, two languages, parliamentary democracy, health care, and treaties. Match each idea to what it means.

skills.title: Canada's Government and the World
skills.description: Canada's government works with other countries through trade deals, alliances, aid, and promises to protect nature. Match each way to an example.

skills.title: Canada in World Agreements
skills.description: Canada joins groups like the UN, WHO, NATO, and NAFTA. Match each one to what it does and why Canada takes part.

skills.title: Groups Helping Around the World
skills.description: Groups like Doctors Without Borders, the UN, and la Francophonie work on world problems. Match each group to what it does.

skills.title: Helping After Disasters Abroad
skills.description: Canada's government and helper groups sent aid after events like the Haiti earthquake and the tsunami. Match each disaster to how Canada helped.

skills.title: Responses to World Issues
skills.description: Governments, NGOs, and everyday people respond to world problems like disease or child labour in different ways. Match each helper to its response.

skills.title: Nature Problems That Cross Borders
skills.description: Problems like global warming, overfishing, and invasive species need many countries to help. Pick why one country can't fix them alone.

skills.title: Canada, the Holocaust, and Human Rights
skills.description: Canada turned away many Jewish refugees during the Holocaust, and later helped write human rights laws. Match each event or law to what it shows.

skills.title: Canada's Effects on Other Regions
skills.description: Canada's peacekeeping, trade, and school projects change life in other places. Match each action to its effect.

skills.title: Finding Canada's Partners on Maps
skills.description: Canada has close ties with countries like the United States, Japan, and Kenya. Find them on a map and use latitude and longitude to locate their cities.

skills.title: Canada's Trading Partners
skills.description: Canada trades most with close or stable countries that make or buy what it needs. Match each country to why it is a partner.

skills.title: Trade and Canadian Jobs
skills.description: Trade deals, disputes, and low labour costs overseas can change jobs and money in Canada. Match each cause to its economic effect.

skills.title: Global Links and Nature
skills.description: Trade and travel can bring invasive species or cause over-farming, and global projects can plant trees. Match each link to its effect on nature.
